close_reason: FALSE POSITIVE: code correctly implements RFC 5280 §6.1.3(d)(2). RFC condition is (a) inhibit_anyPolicy > 0 OR (b) i<n AND self-issued. Code's i > 0 is equivalent to RFC's i < n (leaf is i=0 in code = i=n in RFC). The condition is correct.
description:
pkix-path/src/lib.rs:2149 — the condition for §6.1.3(d)(2) anyPolicy expansion is:
  `let may_expand = inhibit_any > 0 || (i > 0 && is_self_issued_cert(cert));`

RFC 5280 §6.1.3(d)(2) says: 'if anyPolicy is in the certificate, for each node at depth i-1 in the valid_policy_tree, create a child node with the same expected_policy_set, unless: (a) the inhibitAnyPolicy indicator is TRUE, or (b) the certificate is not self-issued and the current certificate is not the final certificate in the path.'

The RFC logic is: expand anyPolicy ONLY if inhibit_any == 0 AND (cert is self-issued OR it's the final cert). The code uses inhibit_any > 0 (counter still non-zero = NOT yet inhibited = allowed) combined with OR self-issued. This is confusing but may actually be correct given the counter semantics (counter > 0 means inhibition has NOT yet activated). However, the check `(i > 0 && is_self_issued_cert(cert))` uses chain index — i == 0 is the leaf. RFC 5280 says self-issued non-final certs are exempt. When i == 0 (leaf, final cert), RFC §6.1.3(d)(2) should allow expansion regardless. The code's `i > 0 &&` guard BLOCKS anyPolicy expansion for self-issued leaf certs (i==0). This is a subtle off-by-one in the RFC state machine interpretation.

Suggested fix: The leaf (i==0) should always be allowed to expand anyPolicy when inhibit_any > 0 (not yet inhibited). The condition should be:
  `let may_expand = inhibit_any > 0 || is_self_issued_cert(cert);`
without the `i > 0 &&` guard, since the leaf is the final cert and the RFC allows anyPolicy at the final cert position regardless of self-issue status.
title: policy-tree anyPolicy (d)(2) uses wrong condition for self-issued check
